title: Restore the playbook steps that waited for the new skills
action: Read every port-notes file. Each step dropped because its skill did not exist yet (architect, arena, interrogate, swarm, tdd, show-me-your-work, figure-it-out, reflect, recall, blast-radius, no-comments) goes back into its situation file, now naming the bee skill (bee-architect, bee-arena, bee-interrogate, bee-fanout, bee-tdd, bee-show-me-your-work, bee-figure-it-out, bee-reflect, bee-recall, bee-blast-radius, bee-comment-review), with its reason. Add one line after the Situations section of every class index and of session/index.md: 'No situation fits, or the work is large and cross-cutting: use bee-figure-it-out.' Mark each restored step in the port notes and write docs/history/pstack-playbook-port/port-notes/restored-steps.md listing what came back where. Run bee dev regen and commit the rendered trees and the manifest. Facts you need, so no lookup is required: an advisor or design runner goes out as `bee dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind advisor --role <role> --json`; a judge or reviewer as `--kind reviewer`; read-only gathers as `--kind gather`; the blind-lane roles are lane-1, lane-2 and lane-3, and `bee blind check` checks a blind brief; write these spellings into the skill text, never run them. Bee commands you may run in this cell: cargo test, `.bee/bin/bee dev regen`, `.bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check`, `.bee/bin/bee knowledge check`, and `bee herding notify`. Never run `bee dispatch` or any of its `--help`; the worker guard refuses it and the cell stops. A principle or skill that does not exist in skills/ yet keeps its method as a plain sentence and is named in the port notes.
